findings.title: Reset code generated with non-cryptographic PRNG
findings.description: random.randint() uses the `random` module's Mersenne Twister, which is not cryptographically secure and is predictable given enough output. Password reset codes are a security-sensitive secret and must be generated with `secrets` (e.g. secrets.randbelow) to prevent an attacker from predicting or brute-forcing the sequence.

findings.title: RESET_CODE_TTL_MINUTES defined but never enforced
findings.description: The constant RESET_CODE_TTL_MINUTES is declared but no timestamp is stored alongside the code and reset_password() never checks expiry. Reset codes therefore never expire, letting an old/leaked code be used indefinitely.

findings.title: No rate limiting or attempt throttling on reset_password
findings.description: reset_password() allows unlimited attempts to guess a 6-digit code (1,000,000 possibilities) with no lockout, delay, or attempt counter, making online brute-force of the code trivial, especially combined with the fact the code never expires.

findings.title: User enumeration via distinct error on unknown username
findings.description: request_password_reset() raises AuthError('unknown user') when the username doesn't exist, letting an attacker distinguish valid from invalid usernames. It should behave identically (e.g. return without error) regardless of whether the account exists.

findings.title: Non-constant-time comparison of reset code
findings.description: `_reset_codes.get(username) != code` uses standard string comparison, which short-circuits on the first mismatched character, enabling a timing side-channel to help an attacker guess the code faster. Use hmac.compare_digest for the comparison.

findings.title: Reset codes stored only in an in-process dict
findings.description: _reset_codes is a plain module-level dict, not persisted to the database. It will not be shared across multiple worker processes/threads (common in production deployments) and is wiped on any restart, breaking the reset flow and silently losing pending reset requests.

findings.title: Existing sessions/tokens not invalidated after password reset
findings.description: After a successful password reset, any outstanding auth tokens for the user remain valid (the tokens table is untouched). If the password was reset because of a compromised account, an attacker holding a valid token retains access after the reset.

findings.title: No tests for new password reset functionality
findings.description: The diff adds request_password_reset() and reset_password(), including new expiry/security-relevant behavior, but includes no test coverage for the happy path, invalid code, expired code, or unknown user cases.
